svg.text: Open ML Compiler Ecosystem - StableHLO + XLA + Shardy + PJRT - openxla.org
CPU/GPU: LLVM IR - opt - native code (NVPTX, x86, ARM)
GPU: TritonIR emitters for matmul/softmax fusions
TPU: Mosaic/Pallas custom emitters via PJRT plugin
Executable blob + buffer layout for runtime dispatch
Modular: slot in novel HW backend without rewriting framework frontends
Framework graph - StableHLO - XLA HLO - backend codegen - PJRT execute
Step 1: Framework lowers model to StableHLO (static shapes, ~100 HLO ops)
Step 2: Optional Shardy/GSPMD - annotate sharding - propagate - SPMD partition
Step 3: XLA target-independent passes - CSE, fusion, buffer assignment
Step 4: Backend-specific HLO opt - library calls - stream schedule - emit LLVM/Triton
Step 5: PJRT Compile() - ExecuteOnStream() - populate device buffers - XProf trace
Goals: faster execution, lower memory, reduce custom ops, hardware portability
Defragments ML toolchain between frameworks and diverse accelerator backends
Pluggable PJRT plugins per accelerator - modular compiler stack on MLIR
Built on MLIR - layered extensible compiler platform with plug-in HW customization
One portable IR (StableHLO) - one compiler (XLA) - one runtime API (PJRT) - many frameworks and accelerators
Init path: framework export StableHLO - optional sharding - XLA Compile via PJRT plugin
Step path: PJRT ExecuteOnStream - device kernels - collectives - buffer reuse - profile with XProf
Sources: openxla.org - github.com/openxla/xla - StableHLO spec - XLA GPU architecture - Google OSS blog 2023
